title: Which Acceleration Does Inertia Listen To? The Ignatiev High-Latitude Window as an Intra-Modified-Inertia Discriminator, and a Pre-Registered Exact Null for de Sitter-Unruh Modified Inertia
description: Ignatiev (PRL 98, 101101, 2007; PRD 77, 102001, 2008) showed that if modified-inertia (MI) MOND couples to a body's COORDINATE acceleration in the Galactic frame, then twice a year, near the equinoxes, at latitude ~80 deg N/S, the Earth's spin-centripetal and orbital accelerations momentarily cancel, dropping a bench-mounted body's kinematic acceleration below a0 for a fraction of a millisecond and producing a spontaneous-displacement blip -- his full interferometer treatment gives ~1e-14 m (the SHLEM effect). The effect is entirely his; this note asks what it discriminates WITHIN the MI class. We reproduce his window from the kinematic budget (cancellation latitude 79.92 deg against his derived 79 deg 50' = 79.83 deg; window 0.43 ms at a0 = 9.354e-11 m/s^2 canonical, 0.53 ms at the alternative footing 1.136e-10), and reproduce his ~1e-14 m amplitude via the suspension-response bridge dx ~ a0*dt/omega0 (9.9e-15 m canonical / 1.5e-14 m alt at his LIGO omega0 = 4.1 1/s); the naive rigid-body in-window floor is 8.8e-18 m canonical / 1.6e-17 m alt. The window is ROBUST to frame choice: Ignatiev's cancellation budget explicitly includes the Sun's galactocentric acceleration as a vector, and his continuity theorem guarantees at least two exact zeros per year (a prior scalar-magnitude reading claiming the galactocentric term kills the window is identified as wrong and retracted in-text). We then show the de Sitter-Unruh MI framework -- inertia as a response to the dS-Unruh bath at the body's PROPER acceleration, with a committed memory kernel tau_mem = 2Z/H_Lambda = 203 Gyr -- predicts an EXACT null in the SHLEM transient channel by two independent routes: (A) a supported bench mass has proper acceleration g ~ 9.8 m/s^2 at ALL times, unchanged by the kinematic cancellation (the bench mass never enters free fall during the window, so the framework's free-fall sector is never invoked), so the time-tagged transient is zero exactly (the static a0/2g ~ 4.8e-12 canonical / 5.8e-12 alt inertia offset is constant and calibration-absorbed); (B) even if the kinematic variable were (wrongly) fed into the framework's kernel, the 203-Gyr memory averages the millisecond window down by a duty factor 6.7e-23 (canonical; 8.2e-23 alt), to at most ~7e-37 m -- and the kernel-averaged input never leaves the Newtonian regime even instantaneously, so this is a conservative upper bound. The experiment is therefore a KILL-CONDITION-ONLY observable for this framework: a blip at Ignatiev's magnitude and timing falsifies BOTH the proper-acceleration coupling AND the long-memory kernel simultaneously (a working, near-term falsification route this paper hands to the framework's critics); a null kills short-memory Galactic-frame kinematic MI while leaving the framework CONSISTENT BUT NOT CONFIRMED -- the null is shared with modified gravity (whose external-field effect also predicts null on Earth) and with plain Newton, so a null moves no evidential weight toward the framework. The discriminator tests which VARIABLE inertia couples to -- not the value of a0 or Z, which remain posited throughout. Existing laboratory nulls do not discriminate: Gundlach et al. (PRL 98, 150801, 2007) verified F=ma at lateral accelerations of 5e-14 m/s^2, which both readings pass (the framework because proper acceleration is 9.8; kinematic MI because the spin centripetal ~2e-2 m/s^2 exceeds a0 outside the windows). McCulloch's quantized inertia -- also Unruh-based -- generically predicts laboratory-scale anomalies; this framework predicts laboratory nulls, a further intra-Unruh-class distinction. The experiment, proposed in 2007, has never been performed; it requires a LIGO-class displacement sensor (~1e-19 m/rtHz) at ~80 deg latitude (Svalbard 78N; Antarctic Dome A 80.4S). CREDIT: the SHLEM effect and the window analysis are Ignatiev's; the nonlocal-MI class is Milgrom's (1994, Ann. Phys. 229, 384); the interpolation kernel nu(y)=sqrt(1+1/y) is Milgrom's (1999, Phys. Lett. A 253, 273). Novelty coverage caveat: a search found no prior publication of this intra-MI discriminator reading of SHLEM; 'no duplicate found' is not 'none exists'. Every load-bearing number is produced by the committed, exit-0 script shlem_discriminator.py (which independently reproduces Ignatiev's latitude and amplitude).
notes: Referee-graded writeup (draft -> 3-reviewer adversarial panel [physics/honesty/citation] -> revise). The physics panel extracted and read Ignatiev 2008 (PRD 77, 102001) in full text and corrected a SEVERE error in the draft's frame-fork section: the claim that an absolute-frame reading has no window (scalar-magnitude sum) is WRONG -- Ignatiev's cancellation is vectorial in the Galactic frame with the event time free, his budget explicitly includes the galactocentric term, and his continuity theorem guarantees >= 2 exact zeros/year; the correction STRENGTHENS the discriminator (the blip side loses its escape hatch; the operative fork is Galactic-frame vs invariant-a0, the latter internally inconsistent by his Eqs. 2.1-2.3). The panel also added the two-sector variable-assignment paragraph (free-fall vs supported worldlines; the bench mass never enters free fall during the window), the suspension-response bridge quantitatively reproducing Ignatiev's 1e-14 m, and both-footings duty factors. Kill-condition-only framing enforced throughout: a null moves no weight toward the framework. Both a0 footings on every dimensional number; a0's value and Z remain postulates. Companion to MI Field Theory Results 2026 (10.5281/zenodo.21403470), the relational sigma-spread paper (10.5281/zenodo.21421896, the 203-Gyr kernel commitment), and the inverted-black-hole duality note (10.5281/zenodo.20947913, the free-fall sector). https://github.com/carlzimmerman/zimmerman-formula
